root.name: Modern Defense: Kotov Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 g6 2. c4 Bg7 3. Nc3 d6 4. e4 Nc6

overview: Black meets White's big centre with ...Nc6 to hit d4 and prepare ...e5. After 5.Be3 e5 6.d5 Nce7 the centre locks and Black has a King's Indian-style structure with ...f5 or ...c6 breaks. White can also play 5.Nf3 e5 or 5.d5 Nb8, gaining space. Black is cramped but solid.

white_ideas.idea: Play d5 to gain space and lock the centre, then expand with Nge2, f3 and Qd2.
Build with Be3, Nf3 and Be2 and keep the centre flexible.

black_ideas.idea: Challenge d4 with ...e5 and, after d5, reroute the knight with ...Nce7.

typical_structures.structure: King's Indian-type locked centre: pawns on c4, d5, e4 against e5 and d6.

character.notes: Black takes a cramped but resilient position and waits to strike with ...f5. Not especially forcing.

soundness.notes: Playable; White may keep a space edge.

structure.notes: After d5 the centre locks, giving a closed King's Indian-type structure.

approach.notes: Modern Defense lines are less common but played by good players; standard rather than offbeat.

level.notes: Needs good judgement of when to break; theory is moderate.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5.d5
sublines_that_differ.how: White gains space at once and Black's knight has lost two tempi.

character.reason: Locked centre with wing play, neither forcing nor a fortress.

structure.reason: After d5 e5 the centre is locked.

approach.reason: A less common line that strong players do play.

level.reason: Middlegame plans matter more than theory.

plans.reason: Black lets White take the centre and attacks it.
